subject: Multi-cloud catalog entry: slab prioritization & co-sell asks
messages:
From: Jasmine Liu <jasmine.liu@redwood.ai>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 18 May 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Multi-cloud catalog entry: slab prioritization & co-sell asks

Hi team,

I ran a quick pass on the marketplace matrix and traffic estimates (attachments) and want us to converge on a prioritization that is executable across AWS/Azure/GCP. High-level ask below — would like decisions by EOD Thursday so we can lock offer descriptions for legal + partner intake next week.

Top-level proposal (what I think is realistic):
- Entry slabs (apply per cloud):
  1) Core Hosted SKU: global hosted API offering (single listing, regional availability flags)
  2) Reserved/Dedicated SKU: named SKU for reserved capacity (per-cloud variant, requires separate entitlement)
  3) Edge/Region-Limited SKU: smaller footprint bundles for specific regions (PR/EMEA/Asia pilots)

Key decisions we need from this thread:
- Per-cloud region priority (3 top regions each) — affects listing regions and initial co-sell focus
- SKU naming & packaging differences (single global SKU vs cloud-specific offer variants)
- Co-sell trigger criteria we surface on the listing (minimum ARR, joint customer registration, use-case templates)

Proposed region priorities (initial thought):
- AWS: us-east-1, us-west-2, eu-west-1
- Azure: eastus, westeurope, southeastasia
- GCP: us-central1, europe-west1, asia-east1

Attachments: marketplace_matrix_v1.xlsx, region_traffic_estimates.csv (see tab "quick-slab").

If you have alternative constraints (procurement, pricing, SKU naming guidelines) call them out here. I’ll compile and send a short forward to partner ops for AWS/Azure/GCP to validate co-sell mechanics.

Thanks — Jasmine

--
Jasmine Liu
GTM Marketplace Lead | Redwood Inference
https://redwood.ai

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Jasmine Liu <jasmine.liu@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 18 May 2027 13:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Multi-cloud catalog entry: slab prioritization & co-sell asks

Thanks for the clear asks, Jas — good framing. Quick response and a proposed mapping (attaching a single-page PDF with the logic). Main points: 

1) Regions — agree largely with your list but swap one region for redundancy:
   - AWS: us-east-1, eu-west-1, ap-southeast-1 (we should include ap-southeast early for APAC partner momentum)
   - Azure: eastus, westeurope, southeastasia
   - GCP: us-central1, europe-west1, asia-south1

2) SKU model:
   - Keep one canonical "Hosted" offer for the Marketplace listing (cleans up telemetry and reduces confusion). Under that offer, publish 3 consumption SKUs (Host-Std, Host-Pro, Host-Enterprise) to capture typical PLG -> expansion motion.
   - Dedicated/Reserved should be separate offer(s) per cloud to ensure entitlement flow and billing alignment (examples: "Reserved - AWS", "Reserved - Azure").
   - Edge/Region-Limited to be packaged as "marketplace pilot" SKUs limited by region.

3) Co-sell triggers (suggestions to present to partners):
   - Minimum committed ARR: $50k ARR (waivable via partner intro)
   - Active joint opportunity recorded in partner portal + joint solution brief
   - For AWS: co-sell registration + ISV Accelerate opt-in (ask Mike/Hanson about exact intake form)

4) Procurement/legal constraints:
   - Need separate EULA clause for Dedicated offers (data isolation language) — feed to legal intake next week.

I attached karthik_entry_proposal.pdf with a sample offer naming convention and a mapping table for which SKU maps to which region. If you want, I can produce a condensed set of offer descriptions for partner intake.

-Karthik

From: Jasmine Liu <jasmine.liu@redwood.ai>

Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 19 May 2027 10:03:00 -0700
Subject: Fwd: Multi-cloud catalog entry: slab prioritization & co-sell asks

Mike — forwarding a short internal thread and our proposed entry model. We’re trying to align on: 1) AWS listing configuration (single hosted offer + AWS-specific reserved SKU variants), and 2) co-sell intake mechanics / Accelerate opt-in.

Attached: marketplace_matrix_v1.xlsx, karthik_entry_proposal.pdf

Two quick questions for you:
1) For AWS co-sell, is the recommended approach: publish a single Marketplace offer with multiple consumption SKUs + a separate Reserved offer for "Reserved - AWS"? Any reasons you’d advise against this structure?
2) For Accelerate/ISV co-sell, what’s the minimum set of artifacts we should prepare for an intake (registration form, joint solution brief, SAML/SSO doc)?

Appreciate a quick reply — we’d like to capture your guidance in the partner intake doc and submit by next Monday.

Best,
Jasmine

Subject: Re: Multi-cloud catalog entry: slab prioritization & co-sell asks — internal consensus + next steps

Thanks everyone — quick summary and actions so we can move to legal + partner intake early next week.

Decision summary (agreed):
- Regions: AWS (us-east-1, eu-west-1, ap-southeast-1); Azure (eastus, westeurope, southeastasia); GCP (us-central1, europe-west1, asia-south1).
- SKU model: single canonical Hosted offer with three consumption SKUs (Host-Std, Host-Pro, Host-Enterprise). Dedicated/Reserved will be separate per-cloud offers. Edge pilots will be region-limited SKUs.
- Co-sell triggers: propose $50k ARR minimum but allow partner waiver via documented joint registration; require at minimum a partner-logged opportunity and brief.

Action items:
1) Jasmine — finalize short offer descriptions (350–500 words) for the Hosted SKUs and attach to partner intake doc. Due: Monday 09:00 PT. (attachment: draft_offer_descriptions.md)
2) Karthik — confirm nomenclature for Reserved offers and hand to legal for EULA clause edits. Due: Monday 17:00 PT.
3) Marissa — place a placeholder entry in HubSpot for the intake (HD-8872) and attach the matrix. Due: Monday 12:00 PT.

If we get Mike/Hanson feedback today we will incorporate before intake. Otherwise we proceed on Monday and raise any country-specific blocking issues in the intake form.

—Marissa
